req.title: Return 404 for unknown routes
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 for any path not matching a defined route.

doc.reasoning: R-HTTPBIN-036 requires that any path not matching a defined route returns HTTP 404. The three violations were: test[0] (test_unknown_path_returns_404), test[6] (test_deeply_nested_unknown_path_returns_404), and test[11] (test_unknown_path_delete_method_returns_404) were marked kind=negative but heuristic=EP. The rule requires that negative kind tests do not use EP heuristic. Fix: change heuristic for those three tests from EP to NEG, which correctly reflects that these are negative tests verifying the error pathway (404 for unknown routes). All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_unknown_path_returns_404
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Path /this-path-does-not-exist is not registered as a route
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET request to /this-path-does-not-exist
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 404
trace: R-HTTPBIN-036: unknown routes must return 404
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/this-path-does-not-exist')
assert r.status_code == 404, f'Expected 404 but got {r.status_code}'

tests.name: test_known_route_get_returns_200_not_404
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Path /get is a registered route accepting GET
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send GET request to /get
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 200
trace: R-HTTPBIN-036: defined routes must NOT return 404
Confirms the 404 logic does not fire for valid routes
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/get')
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200 but got {r.status_code}'
assert r.status_code != 404, 'Known route /get must not return 404'
